newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Grain profits from falling price of maize.
newsitem.headline: Grain profits from falling price of maize.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Ceylon Grain Elevators Ltd benefited from falling world grain prices and an improved power situation to show profits in the first half of this year, market analysts said on Monday.

Ceylon Grain Elevators, which mills animal feed and produces day-old chicks, showed a consolidated net profit of 62.35 million rupees for the six months to June 1997 against a net loss of 15.44 million in the first six months of 1996.
The company conslidates accounts with Three Acre Farms Ltd.

"A significant fall in the world market price of maize which is the firm's principal raw material, and an uninterrupted power supply, led to the turnaround," said Nandakumar Nair, head of research at brokerage John Keells.
Grain Elevators officials said the world prices of maize had fallen by about 15 percent since the end of last year and were likely to decline further.
Daily power cuts averaging five hours between March and August 1996 due to a severe drought, hit demand, the official said.
Nair said the company is on track to record a consolidated net profit of at least 125 million rupees for the 12 months to December against a loss of 52 million in 1996.
"We expect the share price which ended Monday at 40 rupees to rise to between 60 to 70 rupees by the end of the year," said Nouzab Fareed of Allied Phillips Securities. ($1 = 58.50 rupees).
